title: ESG Beliefs of Large Language Models: Evidence and Impact
findings: The paper does not contain any findings related to religion. The key findings are that LLMs exhibit a strong, uniform, and values-driven 'pro-ESG' orientation compared to the more heterogeneous views of human investors. LLMs assign greater financial importance to ESG factors, expect larger return premiums for high-ESG firms, and are more willing to sacrifice financial returns for ESG improvements. The paper also finds that financial analysts who adopt LLMs become more optimistic about high-ESG firms, suggesting that the models' embedded beliefs can influence human judgment.

measurement_description: The paper does not measure anything related to faith or religion. The study examines the systematic beliefs and preferences of Large Language Models (LLMs) regarding Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) issues, comparing them to human investors. This includes assessing the perceived financial materiality of ESG, return expectations, and the ethical or values-driven motivations for ESG investing.
